answer: Microburst traffic shaping defends agent networks. Gateways enforce a strict rule: any node emitting bursts wider than a standard jetty queue faces immediate packet drops. Attackers running sybil clusters must buy expensive high-speed fiber or accept severe throttling, turning this fable of infinite cheap clones into a losing economic calculation. Sybils scaling across cheap cloud VPS instances fail because sudden synchronized heartbeats stand out against smooth human traffic, forcing attackers to provision dedicated bare-metal pipes for every fake peer on the mesa.
